title: When a motion-controlled game misses your swing, what tells you whether you mistimed it or the game lagged?
author: One_Muscle_6651
selftext:
I’m building a browser cricket game where you swing in front of your webcam to bat. The moment I’m trying to get right is the *miss*. If I swing late and get bowled, fair enough. If I swing on time but the bat starts moving after my hands have already gone through, that same wicket feels awful.

For people who played Wii Sports, Kinect, or VR sports games, what made a swing feel right? Was it seeing the bat start moving the instant you moved, hearing the crack exactly at contact, or seeing the ball go where you aimed?

I’m especially curious about consistency. Could you get used to a small, predictable delay? What happened when one swing felt instant and the next felt late? And when you missed, was there a game that made it obvious what to change on the next try?

I’d love a specific example. Even something as simple as “I always had to swing early in \_\_\_” tells me a lot.
